profiles.  On the conventional normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the
sharp first place form $\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\lceil
n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$, i.e. the usual $2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$, pair form
quoted in the literature. ∎

10.text:
For a profile write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}
\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|, \qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $O$ and can put
every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above the whole of $O$.
Hence in the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

A set can be made $>t$--loaded in the worst case iff
$\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and its worst outside charge is
$n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$.  Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.

$k\ge2$.  We may take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t .
$$

In particular $k=2$ gives $\le f_{3}+f_{4}\le2t$, $k=3$ gives
$\le f_{4}\le t$.

$k\le1$ is the essential case.  If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le4t$ and

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 4t-t=3t .
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only
worst-case admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair and no triple is $>t$-loaded,
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$, the unique $>t$-admissible set in the
worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and we can make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle
$n=4t=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ phenomenon.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the bound $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.
For $m=4$, $t=20$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{\,>t}=(m-1)t=3t=60
$$

agents, i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{\ge t+1}=61$ in the $t+1$ book-keeping,
attained on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and on the balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profiles.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}$ singleton
guarantee.

On the customary minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ the
bound is written in the familiar first-place form.  With
$j_{0}$ a least first place item $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ satisfies
$p_{i}(O_{0})\ge t+1$ for $i\in O_{0}$ and $c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le
n_{0}/4=t+1=21$, i.e. $20$ in the strict $>t$ wording.  In pair
language

$$
\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\frac{n_{0}}2=2(t+1)=42,
$$

$2t=40$ in the loose $>t$ notation, which is the $n_{0}=4(t+1)$
normalisation of the $3t$ uniform singleton bound above. ∎

1.text:
For a profile write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|,\;f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge
f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and $\sum f_{i}=n$.  In the worst ordering we may
assume for $|O|\ge2$

\begin{equation*}
p_{O}(i)=f_{i},\qquad i\in O,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad j\notin O ,
\end{equation*}
and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$, $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and
$\max _{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.  Hence, up to the $+1$ slack,
$O$ can be made $>t$ loaded iff $\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and then
$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$.
Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.

If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The only essential
case is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded in the
worst case and the only $>t$ admissible set which can be forced is a
singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  Now

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is best possible.  Indeed with

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded and with the obvious
ordering every voter whose first choice is $2,3,4$ can be made to rank
$2,3,4$ above $1$.  Hence for $O_{*}=\{1\}$

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and the same bound is obtained on the $4t$-cycle $f_{i}\equiv t$,
$n=4t$, for which $n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

In particular

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  For $m=4$

$$
u_{n{\rm -free}}^{*}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20$,
$n=81$, the usual $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile, and with the
strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ bookkeeping $u_{*}=3t+1=61$.  This is the
$n$-free, $n-\max f_{i}$ singleton guarantee.  On the conventional
minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$ the three set
$O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$ a least first place item can
be chosen and

$$
c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1,
$$

i.e. $21$ first place votes, $20$ in the strict $>t$ wording, and in
the usual pair language $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2
=2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ in the loose $>t$ notation, the familiar
$n/4$–first-place, $n/2$–pair $u\approx2t$ form of the same estimate.
The $60=3t$ value is the $n$-free uniform form of this bound. ∎

6.text:
Write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$,
$\sum f_{i}=n$.  For $O\ne\varnothing$ put

$p_{i}(O)=|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}|$, 
$c_{j}(O)=|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}|,\;j\notin O$ .

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep the first choice inside $O$ and
put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$.  In the
worst case

$\min_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$,
and for a singleton $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$, $\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we can take $O$ to be the
$k$ $t+1$ first place items.  Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ and

$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t$,

so $k=2$ gives $\le2t$, $k=3$ gives $\le t$ and $k=4$ gives $0$.
The only obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le4t$ and with $i_{0}=\arg\max f_{i}$

$\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(\{i_{0}\})=n-f_{i_{0}}\le 4t-t=3t$.

If $k=1$ put $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$.  No $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ can be $>t$ loaded in the worst case, the only worst case
admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$, $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ and

$\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t$,

with $c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}$ attainable by ranking $j$ above $1$ for every
voter whose first choice is $j$.  The bound is attained for

$f_{1}=t+1,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1$,

e.g. for $t=20$

$f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\;n=81$,

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  Then $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$ for
every pair, no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$ loaded and $O^{*}=\{1\}$ is the unique
suitable set.  The adversary can make

$c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,$

agents prefer $j$ to $1$, and

$\displaystyle \min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le3t$

for every profile, with equality on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and
on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile $n=4t$.  Hence in the
$n$-free, i.e. $n$-independent, sense

$u_{\rm uni}(m,t)=(m-1)t$,

and for $m=4$, $t=20$,

$u_{\rm uni}=3t=60$

agents, $61$ in the $\ge t+1$ book-keeping, can be forced to rank an
outside item above the chosen set and $60$ is best possible.  In
particular $u_{1}^{*}(P)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le3t$ and $3t$ is the uniform
singleton first-place guarantee.

Remark.  On the conventional minimal feasible normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ the three set $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with
$j_{0}$ a least first place item can be made $>t$ loaded and
$c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1$.  This is the familiar
$n_{0}/4$ first-place, $n_{0}/2$ pair, form
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, i.e. $2t=40$
in the loose $>t$ notation, which is the $3t=60$ uniform bound written
on the $n=4t$ resp. $n=4(t+1)$ normalisation. ∎

3.text:
For a profile write
$f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$,  $\sum f_{i}=n$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge 
f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{i}(O)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|\ge f_{i},\qquad
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_{i}(O)=f_{i},\,i\in O$ and can
put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, i.e. in the
worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\!\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
\tag{*}
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items.  Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ and by $(*)$

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

$2t$ for $k=2$, $t$ for $k=3$, $0$ for $k=4$.  The only obstruction is
$k\le1$.

If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le4t$ and with $i_{0}=\arg\max f_{i}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(\{i_{0}\})=n-f_{i_{0}}\le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4
\Big\rceil\le 3t .
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$
can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case because every such $O$
contains an $i$ with $f_{i}\le t$.  The only worst case admissible set
is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$ for which $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic orders.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ij},m_{ji}\}\ge21$, so
no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$-loaded.  The unique suitable set in the worst
case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ with $p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t$ and the adversary can
make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$–cycle
$n=4t=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O\;{\rm $>t$--loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
     \le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the bound $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.
In particular

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}= (m-1)t =3t,
$$

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $m=4,\;t=20$, attained by the
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ first-place profile and by the balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle.  With the strict $\ge t+1$
book-keeping this is the familiar $u=(m-1)(t+1)-3=61$, $63$ in the
loose $(m-1)(t+1)$ notation.  On the canonical normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the $t+1=21\approx20$ first-place,
$2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form usually quoted in the literature. ∎

8.text:
For the first place numbers write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|\ge f_{i},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

In the worst order the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $i\in O$
and put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, so
that up to the usual $+1$ slack

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (m-k)t .
$$

The only obstruction is $k=1$.  Then $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le
t$ and no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case.  The
only $>t$-admissible set which can be forced is the singleton
$O_{*}=\{1\}$ and

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t ,
$$

with equality for the first–place extremal profile

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

e.g. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
cyclic first choices.  On this profile every $|O|\ge2$ contains an item
with $f_{i}=t<t+1$ so no pair and no triple is $>t$–loaded; the unique
$>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and the
adversary can make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  With the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four
cycle $n=4t=80$ we have the same

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=3t .
$$

Hence in the $n$-free uniform formulation

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible.  For $m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}=60$ agents for $t=20$, the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
profile being the tight extremal example.  In the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ bookkeeping this is the familiar $u=(m-1)(t+1)-3$,
$61$ agents for $t=20$, the $3t=60$ value above.  On the canonical
normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)$ this is the usual $t+1=21\approx20$
first-place, $2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form. ∎

5.text:
For a profile write $f_{i}$ for the number of first place votes of $i$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\},\qquad 
c_{O}(j)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$, $i\in O$, and can
put every voter whose first choice lies outside $O$ above $O$.  Hence in
the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)\ge\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad
\max_{j\notin O}c_{O}(j)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$ $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}c_{\{i\}}(j)=n-f_{i}$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$ .  If $k\ge2$ we can take the $k$ $t+1$
large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{O}(j)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}\le (m-k)t ,
$$
e.g. $f_{3}+f_{4}\le2t$ for $k=2$.  The essential case is $k\le1$,
i.e. $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be
made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only worst-case admissible
set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  For the singleton

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{O_{*}}(j)=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for the first–place extremal

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair and no triple can be made
$>t$–loaded, the unique worst–case suitable set is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and in
the worst ranking

$$
c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents can be made to rank $j$ above $1$.  On the $4t$–cycle
$f_{i}\equiv t$, $n=4t=80$, the same bound $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ is obtained.
Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the $(m-1)t$ bound is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.
In particular

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t$ for $m=4$.  For $t=20$ this is the
uniform $n$–free guarantee

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t=60
$$

agents, $61$ on the strict $\ge t+1$ book–keeping, $n-\max f_{i}=60$
on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
four–cycle.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}\le3n/4$ singleton form of the
usual $n_{0}=m(t+1)$ estimate $ \min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=
\lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$, i.e. $2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ in the
loose $>t$ notation, the $u\approx2t$ pair bound commonly quoted in the
literature.  The $60=3t$ value is the $n$–independent $ (m-1)t$
singleton worst case. ∎

11.text:
Write $f_{i}$ for the ordinary first place numbers
$\sum_{i}f_{i}=n$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\},\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep a voter whose first choice is in $O$
on his first choice in $O$ and can put every voter whose first choice is
outside $O$ above the whole of $O$.  Up to the $t+1$ slack this can be
taken as

$$
p_{i}(O)=f_{i},\;i\in O,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad |O|\ge2,
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le(m-k)t .
$$

In particular $k=2$ gives $\le f_{3}+f_{4}\le2t$, $k=3$ gives
$\le f_{4}\le t$ and $k=4$ gives $0$.  The only obstruction to a
$|O|\ge2$ $>t$-loaded set is $k\le1$.

Let $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$.  Then every
$O$ with $|O|\ge2$ contains an $i$ with $f_{i}\le t$ and in the worst
ranking $p_{i}(O)=f_{i}\le t$.  The only worst-case admissible set is a
singleton, up to relabelling $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ as
soon as $n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound can be attained.  The extremal first place profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

e.g. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic orders.  On this profile
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$ for every pair, so no pair and no triple
can be made $>t$-loaded; the unique $>t$-loaded set in the worst case
is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  Putting every voter whose first choice is $2,3$ or
$4$ above $1$ gives

$$
c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and $p_{1}(\{1\})=81>t$.  With the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle
$n=4t=80$ the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t=60$ is obtained.

If a Condorcet winner $w$ exists $f_{j}\le t$, $j\ne w$, and
$n-f_{w}\le3t$; if no Condorcet winner exists $f_{i}\le t$ for all $i$,
$n\le4t$ and $n-\max f_{i}\le3t$.  Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
cyclic profiles show the bound is best possible in the $n$-free
uniform sense.  For $m=4$,

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $61$ in the strict $\ge t+1$
book-keeping $n-\max f_{i}\le3(t+1)-3$.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}$
singleton guarantee $u=n-\max f_{i}\le3t$, the $3n/4$ form of the
usual $u\approx(m-1)t$ estimate.

On the conventional minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$
the three-set $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$ a least first
place item can be forced, $c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1$,
and in the usual pair language $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=
n_{0}/2=2(t+1)$, i.e. the familiar $2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ in the
$\ge t+1$ convention, the $n_{0}=4(t+1)$ normalisation of the $3t$
uniform bound above. ∎

15.text:
For a profile write

$f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $\sum_{i}f_{i}=n$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge
f_{4}$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

\begin{equation*}
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|\ge f_{i},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
\end{equation*}
For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep a voter whose first choice lies in
$O$ on his first choice in $O$ and can make every voter whose first
choice lies outside $O$ put the outside item above $O$.  In the worst
case we may therefore put

\[
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
\]

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

\[
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{\{i\}}(j)=n-f_{i},
\]

up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ slack.  Put
$k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items and

\[
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
\tag{1}
\]

so that $k=2$ gives $\le 2t$, $k=3$ gives $\le t$ and $k=4$ gives $0$.
The only essential regime is $k\le 1$.

If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le 4t$ and with $i_{0}=\arg\max f_{i}$

\[
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(\{i_{0}\})=n-f_{i_{0}}
      \le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil\le 3t,
\]

with equality for the $t,t,t,t$ four–cycle $n=4t$.

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$ can
be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only $>t$–admissible set
which can be forced is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

\[
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t,
\]

and the bound is attained for the first–place extremal profile

\[
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
\]

e.g. for $t=20$

\[
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
\]

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic orders.  On this profile no pair and no triple can be made
$>t$–loaded, the unique $>t$–admissible set in the worst case is
$O_{*}=\{1\}$ and the adversary can make

\[
c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
\]

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  In particular

\[
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 3t,
\]

and $3t$ is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.  Hence with
the loose $>t$ convention

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
\]

and for $m=4$

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t,
\]

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=61$ on the
strict $\ge t+1$ book–keeping, and the extremal profile is the
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$, $n=81$,  and the balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
four-cycle, $n=80$, on which $u_{1}^{*}(P)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=3t$.
This is the $n-\max f_{i}\le 3n/4$ singleton guarantee, the $n$–free
$(m-1)t$ form of the usual core estimate.

Remark.  On the customary minimal feasible normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$ the three–set
$O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$ a least first–place item can
be chosen.  Then $c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1$ and
$p_{i}(O_{0})\ge t+1$, $i\in O_{0}$, i.e. in first–place language

\[
\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\Big\lceil\frac{n_{0}}4\Big\rceil
=t+1=21,
\]

$20$ in the strict $>t$ wording, and in the usual pair language

\[
\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\frac{n_{0}}2=2(t+1),
\]

i.e. $u_{2}=2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ in the strict $\ge t+1$ convention,
the familiar $n/4$ first–place, $n/2$ pair, bound quoted in the
literature.  Up to the inessential $+1$ this is the $3t=60$ singleton
bound written on the $n=4t$, resp. $n=4(t+1)$, normalisation. ∎

12.text:
For a profile put $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}
\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$,

\begin{equation*}
p_{i}(O)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O,
\end{equation*}
and for $|O|\ge2$ we may in the worst case put
$p_{i}(O)=f_{i}$ and $c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$ and for a singleton
$c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.  Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can
take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}\le (m-k)t$,

so that $k=2$ gives $\le 2t$ and $k\ge3$ gives $\le t$.  The only
essential regime is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded
in the worst case and the only worst-case admissible set is a singleton
$O^{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  For a singleton
$p_{O^{*}}(i_{0})=n>t$ and

\[
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t,
\]

and the bound is attained.  In fact

\[
u(P)=\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le(m-1)t,
\]

and for $m=4$

\[
u_{\rm uni}(P)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 3t .
\]

The extremal first place profile is

\[
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
\]

i.e. for $t=20$

\[
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
\]

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic orders.  On this profile no pair and no triple is $>t$
loaded, the unique $>t$ admissible set in the worst case is
$O^{*}=\{1\}$ and in the worst ordering

\[
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
\]

so $60$ agents can be forced to rank $2,3$ or $4$ above $1$, and no
smaller number will do for all profiles.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
four-cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ singleton worst
case.  In the strict $\ge t+1$ book keeping this is $u_{\rm uni}=3(t+1)-3
=61$, i.e. the familiar $u_{\rm uni}=(m-1)t$ uniform, $n$-free,
$ n-\max f_{i}$ bound.

Remark.  On the canonical minimal feasible normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$ the three-set $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with
$j_{0}$ a least first-place item can be chosen.  Then
$c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1$ and
$p_{i}(O_{0})\ge t+1$, $i\in O_{0}$, i.e. the sharp first-place form

\[
\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\Big\lceil\frac{n_{0}}4\Big\rceil
=t+1=21,
\]

$20$ in the strict $>t$ wording, and in the usual pair language
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, i.e. $2t=40$
in the loose $>t$ notation.  This is the $n_{0}=4(t+1)$ normalisation
of the $3t=60$ singleton, $n-\max f_{i}$, uniform bound above. ∎

public_text.7:
Let $f_i$ be first place numbers, $f_1\ge f_2\ge f_3\ge f_4$, $\sum f_i=n$, and for $O\neq\varnothing$

$p_O(i)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_O(v)\},\qquad c_O(j)=\#\{v:j\succ_v O\},\ j\notin O$.

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_O(i)=f_i$ and make every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ rank that outside item above $O$, so in the worst case

\[
\min_{i\in O}p_O(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_i,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i ,
\]

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$ $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and $\max_{j\ne i}c_{\{i\}}(j)=n-f_i$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_i\ge t+1\}$ with $t+1=21$.  
If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$–large items and
$\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i=\sum_{i>k}f_i\le (4-k)t$,
so $k=2$ gives $\le2t$, $k\ge3$ gives $\le t$.

The essential regime is $k\le1$.  Then no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can be
$>t$–loaded in the worst case, because every such $O$ contains an $i$ with
$f_i\le t$.  The only worst-case admissible set is a singleton $O=\{i_0\}$
with $f_{i_0}=\max_i f_i$.  Then

\[
p_{\{i_0\}}(i_0)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_0}c_{\{i_0\}}(j)=n-f_{i_0}=f_2+f_3+f_4\le3t .
\]

Hence for every profile

\[
\min_O\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)\le n-\max_i f_i\le3t,
\]

and the bound is $n$-free.

It is attained.  With
$f_1=t+1$, $f_2=f_3=f_4=t$, $n=4t+1$, i.e. for $t=20$
$f_1=21$, $f_2=f_3=f_4=20$, $n=81$,
$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge21$,
so no $|O|\ge2$ can be $>t$–loaded; the unique $>t$–admissible set in
the worst case is $O^*=\{1\}$ and the adversary can make
$c_{O^*}(j)=n-f_1=81-21=60$ for $j=2,3,4$.
The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile $n=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_i=60$.

If a Condorcet winner $w$ exists then $f_j\le t$ for $j\ne w$ and
$n-f_w\le60$; if no Condorcet winner exists then $f_i\le t$ for all $i$
and $n-\max f_i\le60$.  So $u=3t$ works for every $n$ and every profile
and $60$ is best possible in the $n$-free formulation.

The $2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ numbers are the $n_0=4(t+1)=84$ normalisation
$\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)=\lceil n_0/4\rceil=t+1$ and
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)=n_0/2=2(t+1)$.  That normalisation
is not part of the statement.  With $n$ unrestricted the quantifiers ask
for a uniform guarantee and the uniform guarantee is the singleton
first-place guarantee $n-\max f_i\le3t$, i.e. $u=3t=60$ for $t=20$, $63$
in the $\ge t+1$ bookkeeping. ∎

Write $f_i$ for the ordinary first place numbers, $f_1\ge f_2\ge f_3\ge f_4$, $\sum f_i=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

\[

\]

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_O(i)=f_i$ on $O$ and can make every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ rank that outside item above the whole of $O$, so in the worst case

\[

\]

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

\[

\]

Put $k=\#\{i:f_i\ge t+1\}= \#\{i:f_i\ge21\}$.

The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$. Then no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$
can be made $>t$-loaded in the worst case, because every such $O$
contains an $i$ with $f_i\le t$. The only admissible worst case set is a
singleton. Up to relabelling $O=\{1\}$ with $f_1\ge t+1$, $f_2,f_3,f_4\le t$
and

\[

\]

\[

\]

i.e. for $t=20$

\[

\]

\]

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$, $\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.
Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.

If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le(m-k)t ,
$$

in particular $\le2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The
essential obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$ can
be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only worst case
admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for the first place extremal profile

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair and no triple is
$>20$-loaded, the unique suitable set in the worst case is
$O^{*}=\{1\}$ and the adversary can make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents prefer $j$ to $1$.  The balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
$4$-cycle $n=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=60$ singleton worst case.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $61$ on the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book-keeping, and the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
profile shows the bound is tight.  In the conventional
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation this is the familiar
$\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$,
i.e. the $2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ pair form, the $3t=60$ singleton bound
written on the $n=4t$ scale. ∎
public_text.2:
For a profile write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}v\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge
f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}v\}\bigr|\ge f_{i},\qquad
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

In the worst adversarial ranking we may put
$p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ for $|O|\ge2$ and $c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$,
$j\notin O$, and for a singleton $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$, $c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.
In particular a set $O$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case iff
$\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and then

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}\; .
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$–large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

so that $k=2$ gives $\le2t$, $k=3$ gives $\le t$ and $k=4$ gives $0$.
The only obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$ and $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no
$|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case. The only
worst–case admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$,
$p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and $n-f_{1}$ can be attained by making every voter whose first
choice is $2,3$ or $4$ rank the chosen outside item above $1$.
The bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

e.g. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  No pair $\{a,b\}$ satisfies
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$, so every $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is
$>t$–inadmissible in the worst case and with the unique admissible
singleton $O^{*}=\{1\}$

$$
p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,
$$

$60$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to $1$.  If
$k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le4t$ and $n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le3t$ with
equality for the $t,t,t,t$ four–cycle $n=4t$.

Hence in the $n$-free uniform sense

\[
\min_{O\;{\rm >t\;loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
   =\min_{i}\bigl[n-f_{i}\bigr]\le (m-1)t,
\]

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible.  For $m=4$

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
\]

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $61$ on the strict $\ge t+1$
book–keeping, and it is attained on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and
the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profiles.  This is the
$n-\max f_{i}\le3n/4$ singleton first–place guarantee.  In the usual
minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$ this is the
familiar normalised form

\[
\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\Big\lceil\frac{n_{0}}4\Big\rceil
=t+1=21\approx20,
\]

i.e. $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$
in the loose $>t$ notation, the $u\approx n/4$ first–place, $u\approx
n/2$ pair, bound normally quoted in the literature.  The $3t=60$
value is its $n$-free $m-1$ form. ∎

\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|, \qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above the whole of $O$.
Hence in the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

A set can be made $>t$--loaded in the worst case iff
$\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and its worst outside charge is
$n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$.  Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.

$k\ge2$.  We may take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t .
$$

$\le f_{4}\le t$.

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 4t-t=3t .
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only
worst-case admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair and no triple is $>t$-loaded,
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$, the unique $>t$-admissible set in the
worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and we can make

$$

and the bound $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{\,>t}=(m-1)t=3t=60
$$

agents, i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{\ge t+1}=61$ in the $t+1$ book-keeping,
attained on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and on the balanced

For a profile write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|,\;f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge
f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and $\sum f_{i}=n$.  In the worst ordering we may
assume for $|O|\ge2$

\begin{equation*}
p_{O}(i)=f_{i},\qquad i\in O,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad j\notin O ,
\end{equation*}
and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$, $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and
$\max _{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.  Hence, up to the $+1$ slack,
$O$ can be made $>t$ loaded iff $\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and then
$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$.
Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.

If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The only essential
case is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded in the
worst case and the only $>t$ admissible set which can be forced is a
singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  Now

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is best possible.  Indeed with

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded and with the obvious
ordering every voter whose first choice is $2,3,4$ can be made to rank
$2,3,4$ above $1$.  Hence for $O_{*}=\{1\}$

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and the same bound is obtained on the $4t$-cycle $f_{i}\equiv t$,
$n=4t$, for which $n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

In particular

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  For $m=4$

$$
u_{n{\rm -free}}^{*}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20$,
$n=81$, the usual $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile, and with the
strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ bookkeeping $u_{*}=3t+1=61$.  This is the
$n$-free, $n-\max f_{i}$ singleton guarantee.  On the conventional
minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$ the three set
$O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$ a least first place item can
be chosen and

$$
c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1,
$$

i.e. $21$ first place votes, $20$ in the strict $>t$ wording, and in
the usual pair language $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2
=2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ in the loose $>t$ notation, the familiar
$n/4$–first-place, $n/2$–pair $u\approx2t$ form of the same estimate.
The $60=3t$ value is the $n$-free uniform form of this bound. ∎

and the bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic orders.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ij},m_{ji}\}\ge21$, so
no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$-loaded.  The unique suitable set in the worst
case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ with $p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t$ and the adversary can
make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$–cycle
$n=4t=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O\;{\rm $>t$--loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
     \le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the bound $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.
In particular

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}= (m-1)t =3t,
$$

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $m=4,\;t=20$, attained by the
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ first-place profile and by the balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle.  With the strict $\ge t+1$
book-keeping this is the familiar $u=(m-1)(t+1)-3=61$, $63$ in the
loose $(m-1)(t+1)$ notation.  On the canonical normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the $t+1=21\approx20$ first-place,
$2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form usually quoted in the literature. ∎

For the first place numbers write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|\ge f_{i},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

In the worst order the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $i\in O$
and put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, so
that up to the usual $+1$ slack

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (m-k)t .
$$

The only obstruction is $k=1$.  Then $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le
t$ and no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case.  The
only $>t$-admissible set which can be forced is the singleton
$O_{*}=\{1\}$ and

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t ,
$$

with equality for the first–place extremal profile

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

e.g. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
cyclic first choices.  On this profile every $|O|\ge2$ contains an item
with $f_{i}=t<t+1$ so no pair and no triple is $>t$–loaded; the unique
$>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and the
adversary can make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  With the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four
cycle $n=4t=80$ we have the same

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=3t .
$$

Hence in the $n$-free uniform formulation

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible.  For $m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}=60$ agents for $t=20$, the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
profile being the tight extremal example.  In the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ bookkeeping this is the familiar $u=(m-1)(t+1)-3$,
$61$ agents for $t=20$, the $3t=60$ value above.  On the canonical
normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)$ this is the usual $t+1=21\approx20$
first-place, $2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form. ∎

Write $f_{i}$ for the ordinary first place numbers
$\sum_{i}f_{i}=n$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\},\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep a voter whose first choice is in $O$
on his first choice in $O$ and can put every voter whose first choice is
outside $O$ above the whole of $O$.  Up to the $t+1$ slack this can be
taken as

$$
p_{i}(O)=f_{i},\;i\in O,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad |O|\ge2,
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le(m-k)t .
$$

In particular $k=2$ gives $\le f_{3}+f_{4}\le2t$, $k=3$ gives
$\le f_{4}\le t$ and $k=4$ gives $0$.  The only obstruction to a
$|O|\ge2$ $>t$-loaded set is $k\le1$.

Let $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$.  Then every
$O$ with $|O|\ge2$ contains an $i$ with $f_{i}\le t$ and in the worst
ranking $p_{i}(O)=f_{i}\le t$.  The only worst-case admissible set is a
singleton, up to relabelling $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ as
soon as $n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound can be attained.  The extremal first place profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

e.g. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic orders.  On this profile
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$ for every pair, so no pair and no triple
can be made $>t$-loaded; the unique $>t$-loaded set in the worst case
is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  Putting every voter whose first choice is $2,3$ or
$4$ above $1$ gives

$$
c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and $p_{1}(\{1\})=81>t$.  With the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle
$n=4t=80$ the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t=60$ is obtained.

If a Condorcet winner $w$ exists $f_{j}\le t$, $j\ne w$, and
$n-f_{w}\le3t$; if no Condorcet winner exists $f_{i}\le t$ for all $i$,
$n\le4t$ and $n-\max f_{i}\le3t$.  Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
cyclic profiles show the bound is best possible in the $n$-free
uniform sense.  For $m=4$,

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $61$ in the strict $\ge t+1$
book-keeping $n-\max f_{i}\le3(t+1)-3$.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}$
singleton guarantee $u=n-\max f_{i}\le3t$, the $3n/4$ form of the
usual $u\approx(m-1)t$ estimate.

On the conventional minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$
the three-set $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$ a least first
place item can be forced, $c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le n_{0}/4=t+1$,
and in the usual pair language $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=
n_{0}/2=2(t+1)$, i.e. the familiar $2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ in the
$\ge t+1$ convention, the $n_{0}=4(t+1)$ normalisation of the $3t$
uniform bound above. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has now converged on the $n$-free first-place reduction.  
Let $f_i=\#\{v:i={\rm top}\}$, $f_1\ge f_2\ge f_3\ge f_4$, $\sum f_i=n$.
For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can force $p_O(i)=f_i$, $i\in O$, and
$\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i$; for a singleton
$p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$, $\max_{j\ne i}c_j(\{i\})=n-f_i$.
Hence in the worst case $O$ can be made $>t$-loaded iff
$\min_{i\in O}f_i\ge t+1$ and then
$\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_i\ge t+1\}$.  
If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ as the $k$ large first-place items and
$\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_i\le(4-k)t$, i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$,
$\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  
The essential obstruction is $k\le1$. Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be forced
$>t$-loaded and the only worst-case admissible set is the singleton
$O_*=\{i_0\}$ with $f_{i_0}=\max f_i$. Then
$p_{O_*}(i_0)=n>t$ and $\max_{j\ne i_0}c_j(O_*)=n-f_{i_0}=f_2+f_3+f_4\le3t$.

The bound is tight.  The extremal first-place profile is
$f_1=t+1,\;f_2=f_3=f_4=t$, $n=4t+1$, e.g. for $t=20$
$f_1=21,\;f_2=f_3=f_4=20,\;n=81$,
$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  No pair satisfies $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge21$,
so no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$-loaded; $O^*=\{1\}$ is the unique suitable set and
the adversary can make $c_j(\{1\})=n-f_1=60=3t$ for $j=2,3,4$.
The balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle $n=80$ gives the same

The first-place reduction is the controlling factor. Write $f_i=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_1\ge f_2\ge f_3\ge f_4$, $\sum f_i=n$. For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep $p_O(i)=f_i$ on $O$ and can make every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ rank that outside item above $O$; for a singleton $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and $\max_{j\ne i}c_j(\{i\})=n-f_i$.
Let $k=\#\{i:f_i\ge t+1\}$. If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and in the worst case $\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i=\sum_{i>k}f_i\le(4-k)t$, i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$, $\le t$ for $k\ge3$. The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.

* $k=0$: $f_i\le t$, $n\le4t$, $n-\max f_i\le3t$, equality on the $t,t,t,t$ four-cycle.
* $k=1$, say $f_1\ge t+1$, $f_2,f_3,f_4\le t$. No $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$-loaded in the worst case; the only worst-case admissible set is the singleton $O_*=\{1\}$. Then $p_{O_*}(1)=n>t$ and $\max_{j\ne1}c_j(O_*)=n-f_1=f_2+f_3+f_4\le3t$.

The bound is tight on the first-place extremal profile
$f_1=t+1$, $f_2=f_3=f_4=t$, $n=4t+1$,
e.g. $t=20$: $f_1=21$, $f_2=f_3=f_4=20$, $n=81$,
$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three other cyclic first choices. No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$, so no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$-loaded, the unique $>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^*=\{1\}$ and the adversary can force
$c_j(O^*)=n-f_1=3t$, $j=2,3,4$.
Hence $\min_O\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)\le n-\max_i f_i\le(m-1)t$ for every profile and $(m-1)t$ is best possible uniformly in $n$.

For $m=4$, $t=20$ the $n$-free uniform guarantee is
$u_{\rm uni}^*=(m-1)t=3t=60$ agents, attained on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile $n=81$ and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four-cycle $n=80$. In the strict $\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is $61$, i.e. $60$ in the loose $>t$ wording used in the statement.

The $u\approx2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$, numbers quoted by several colleagues are the same estimate written on the conventional minimal feasible normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)=4(t+1)=84$. On $n_0$ we can remove a least first-place item, $O_0=[4]\setminus\{j_0\}$, with $c_{j_0}(O_0)=f_{j_0}\le n_0/4=t+1$ and $p_i(O_0)\ge t+1$ on $O_0$; in pair language $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n_0/2=2(t+1)$. That $n_0$ normalisation is not part of the quantifiers “for all $n$ and all profiles”. The problem as stated asks for an $n$-free uniform guarantee, which is the singleton first-place bound $n-\max f_i\le3t$, i.e. $u_{\min}=60$ for $t=20$, $3t$ in general. ∎

p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t ,
$$

and the bound is attainable.  Indeed with

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

no pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$, so no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$
loaded in the worst case and the unique $>t$-admissible set is
$O^{*}=\{1\}$.  Putting every voter whose first choice is $2,3,4$
above $1$ we can obtain

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and $p_{O^{*}}(1)=n>t$.  The balanced $4$-cycle
$f_{i}\equiv t$, $n=4t$, gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ phenomenon.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O\;>t{\rm -loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
      \le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.
In particular

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
$$

the $n-\max f_{i}$ singleton first–place guarantee.  For $m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t .
$$

For $t=20$ this is the uniform $n$–independent guarantee

$$
u_{\min}=3t=60 
$$

agents, i.e. $n-\max f_{i}=60$ on the extremal
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile $f_{1}=21$, $f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20$,
$n=81$, and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle $n=80$.
With the strict $\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is the familiar
$u_{\rm uni}^{\ge t+1}=3t+1=61$, $u_{2}=2(t+1)=42$, $u_{3}=t+1=21$,
in the usual $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ normalisation.  This is the $3t$
singleton, $n-\max f_{i}\le3n/4$, form of the bound. ∎

6.text:
For a profile put $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge
f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

\begin{equation*}
p_{O}(i)=|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}|\ge f_{i}, \qquad 
c_{j}(O)=|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}|,\;j\notin O .
\end{equation*}
In the worst ordering we may take for $|O|\ge 2$ 
$p_{O}(i)=f_{i},\,i\in O$, $ \max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$
and for a singleton $p_{\{i\}}(i)=n$, $\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.
Hence $O$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case iff
$\min_{i\in O}f_{i}\ge t+1$ and then $\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=
n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we may take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$–large items and

\[
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t\le2t ,
\]

$ \le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The only $n$–free obstruction is $k\le1$.
Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded and the only worst–case
admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max f_{i}$,
$p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t$ and

\[
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t .
\]

The bound is best possible.  With $k=1$ the extremal first place
profile is

\[
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
\]

and for $t=20$

\[
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
\]

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge
t+1$, so no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the unique
$>t$–admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  The adversary
can make every voter whose first choice is $2,3$ or $4$ rank the chosen
outside item above $1$, whence

\[
p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t,\qquad 
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
\]

and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four–cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

Hence for every profile

\[
\min_{O\;>t{\rm -loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le
(m-1)t,
\]

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
\]

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, $u^{*}=61$ on the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book–keeping $n-\max f_{i}\le3(t+1)-3$.  This is the
$n-\max f_{i}$ singleton first–place guarantee, the familiar $3n/4$
form.  On the canonical normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the
usual $ \lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$, i.e. $2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$, pair
form. ∎

9.text:
For a profile put

$$
f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|,\qquad f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4},
\qquad\sum_{i}f_{i}=n,
$$

$$
p_{O}(i)=|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}| ,\;j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i},\,i\in O$, and
can put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, so in
the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we can take $O$ to be the
$k$ $t+1$–large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The only $n$–free
obstruction is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$-loaded in
the worst case and the only worst case admissible set is a singleton
$O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}
      =f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  Up to relabelling the extremal first place
profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

and with the usual $>t$ convention $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$.  For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair has
$\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$, so no $|O|\ge2$ is $>t$-loaded in the
worst case, the unique $>t$-admissible set is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and the
adversary can make

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents rank $j$ above $1$.  The balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
four-cycle $n=4t$ gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  In
particular

$$
\min_{O\;{\rm >t\;loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
      =n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le3t,
$$

so that with the loose $>t$ convention

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
$$

and for $m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t .
$$

For $t=20$ this is the uniform $n$-independent $n-\max f_{i}$
singleton guarantee

$$
u^{*}=3t=60
$$

agents, attained on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$, $n=81$, and on the
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$, $n=80$, extremal profiles.  In the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is the familiar $u^{*}=3t+1=61$,
i.e. the $n_{0}=4(t+1)=84$ normalisation
$\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$ and
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ in the
loose $>t$ notation.  This is the $3n/4$ singleton first-place
guarantee usually quoted as the $u\approx(m-1)t$ core bound. ∎

3.text:
For a profile let

$$
f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}| ,\qquad f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4},
\qquad \sum f_{i}=n,
$$

and for $O\ne\varnothing $

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\;j\notin O .
$$

In the worst ordering the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $O$ for
$|O|\ge 2$ and can put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$
above the whole of $O$.  Hence in the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad |O|\ge 2,
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we may take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$–large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
            =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le 2t$ for $k=2$, $\le t$ for $k\ge 3$.  The only $n$–free
obstruction is $k\le 1$.  Then no $|O|\ge 2$ can be made $>t$–loaded in the
worst case and the only worst–case admissible set which can be forced is
the singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t ,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  Indeed with

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

no pair and no triple can be made $>t$–loaded and the unique
$>t$–admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  Making every
voter whose first choice is $2,3$ or $4$ rank the chosen outside item
above $1$ gives

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=3t ,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and $p_{O^{*}}(1)=n>t$.  For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices, gives $c_{j}(\{1\})=81-21=60$.
The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four–cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_{i}=3t$.

Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O\;>t{\rm -loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
 \le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, the $n-\max f_{i}\le 3t$
singleton first–place guarantee.  In the usual $\ge t+1$ book–keeping
this is $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t+1=61$, the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ extremal profiles being tight.  On the
conventional normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the familiar
$ \min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$
first–place, $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$,
i.e. $2t=40$ in the loose $>t$ notation, the $3t$ singleton bound written
on the $n=4t$ scale. ∎

5.text:
For a profile let $f_{i}$ be the number of first place votes for $i$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$, and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $O$ and can put
every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, so that in the
worst case

$$\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i}, \qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},$$

and for a singleton

$$p_{\{i\}}(i)=n, \qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we may take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items.  Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ and

$$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
      =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t ,$$

$2t$ for $k=2$, $t$ for $k=3$, $0$ for $k=4$.
The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made
$>t$-loaded in the worst case and the only worst case admissible set
which can be forced is a singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with
$f_{i_{0}}=\max f_{i}$.  Now

$$p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t ,$$

and the bound is best possible.  Indeed with

$$f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,$$

no $O$, $|O|\ge2$, can be made $>t$-loaded and the unique $>t$-admissible
set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  In the worst ordering

$$c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4, $$

and $p_{O^{*}}(1)=n>t$.  For $t=20$

$$f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices, gives

$$p_{\{1\}}(1)=81>20,\qquad c_{j}(\{1\})=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,$$

and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four-cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_{i}=3t$.  Hence for every profile

$$\min_{O}p_{O}(i)\ge t+1\;\Longrightarrow\;
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t, $$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$$u_{\rm uni}^{\,>t}=(m-1)t=3t,$$

i.e. $60$ agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen
set and $60$ is best possible.  In the strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$,
$c_{j}(O)\le u$ book-keeping this is the familiar $u_{\rm uni}=3(t+1)-3
=61$, $u_{\rm uni}=(m-1)t$ in the loose $>t$ wording.  The $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
and the balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profiles are the extremal
examples.  On the conventional normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)$ this is the
usual $t+1$ first-place, $2(t+1)$ pair form $u\approx2t$. ∎

8.text:
For a profile let

$f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$,
$\sum f_{i}=n$, and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr| ,\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i},\,i\in O$, and can
make every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ rank the outside
item above $O$.  In the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$–large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

so that $k=2$ gives $\le f_{3}+f_{4}\le 2t$ and $k\ge3$ gives $\le t$.
The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k=0$, $f_{i}\le t$, $n\le4t$ and with $i_{0}=\arg\max f_{i}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(\{i_{0}\})=n-f_{i_{0}}\le3t .
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$ can
be made $>t$-loaded in the worst case and the only worst-case
admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

$$
p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained for

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic orders.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$,
so no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$-loaded; the unique $>t$-admissible set
in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and in the worst ordering

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

so $60$ agents can be forced to rank $2,3$ or $4$ above $1$, and
$p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t$.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four-cycle $n=4t=80$
gives the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ phenomenon.  Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  In
particular

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
$$

i.e. for $m=4$ the uniform $n$-independent guarantee is $u^{*}=3t$.
For $t=20$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3\times20=60
$$

agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to the chosen set, and
$60$ is tight, e.g. on the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile above.
With the strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is the familiar
$u^{*}=3t+1=61$; the loose $>t$ wording used in the statement is the
$3t=60$ value.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}\le3n/4$ singleton first-place
guarantee.  On the canonical normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the
usual $t+1=21\approx20$ first-place, $2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form.

11.text:
For a profile let $f_{i}$ be the number of first place votes for $i$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$.
Write

$$p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr| ,\qquad

\;j\notin O , $$

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad

\tag{*}
$$

$$

$$

$$

i.e. $\le 2t$ for $k=2$, $\le t$ for $k\ge 3$.  The only $n$–free
obstruction is $k\le 1$.  For $n>t$ a singleton is always $>t$–loaded,

$$
\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$
can be made $>t$–loaded in the worst case and the only worst case
admissible set is $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(\{1\})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le 3t,
$$

and the bound is attainable.  The extremal first–place profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge
t+1$, so no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded.  The unique
$>t$–admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$, $p_{O^{*}}(1)=
81>t$, and by making every voter whose first choice is $2,3$ or $4$
rank the chosen outside item above $1$,

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents can be forced to prefer $j$ to $1$.  The balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four–cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_{i}=3t$.  Hence for every profile with $n>t$

$$
\min_{O\;{\rm >t\;loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}
\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{\,>t}=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}=60$ agents for $t=20$, attained on the
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic
profiles.  In the strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book–keeping this is the
familiar $u_{\rm uni}^{\ge t+1}=3t+1=61$, $n-\max f_{i}\le3t$ in the
loose $>t$ wording.  This is the $n-\max f_{i}$ singleton, i.e. the
$3n/4$, guarantee.

Remark.  On the conventional minimal feasible normalisation
$n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ the three–set $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with $j_{0}$
a least first–place item can be chosen and $c_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}
\le n_{0}/4=t+1$, and in the usual pair language
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, i.e. $2t=40$
in the loose $>t$ notation, the $n_{0}=4(t+1)$ normalisation of the
$3t$ uniform singleton bound above. ∎

1.text:
Write $f_{i}$ for the number of first place votes of $i$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$ and $\sum_{i}f_{i}=n$.
For $O\ne\varnothing $ put 

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $O$ and can
make every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ rank the outside
item above $O$. Hence in the worst case

$$
 \min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
 \max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we may take $O$ to be the
$k$ $t+1$-large items.  Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
       =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le 2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.
The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be
made $>t$-loaded in the worst case and the only worst case admissible
set is a singleton $O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max f_{i}$.
Now

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}
      =f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  The extremal first place profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

and with the usual cyclic ordering

$$
\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=t<t+1
$$

for every pair, so no pair and no triple can be made $>t$-loaded.
The unique $>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

agents can be forced to rank $j$ above $1$.  In particular

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and the $3t$ bound is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.
For $m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(t)=(m-1)t,
$$

and for $t=20$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t=60
$$

agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to the chosen set.
On the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile $n=81$, $f_{1}=21$,
$f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20$,

$$
p_{\{1\}}(1)=81>20,\qquad c_{j}(\{1\})=81-21=60,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and the same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ phenomenon occurs on the balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle $n=4t=80$.  With the strict
$p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is the familiar $u=3t+1=61$
singleton first place guarantee, i.e. $u=(m-1)(t+1)-3$, the
$n_{0}=4(t+1)=84$ normalisation $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=
n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, $2t=40$ in the loose $>t$ wording.  This is the
sharp $n-\max f_{i}\le3n/4$ uniform guarantee. ∎

4.text:
For $i\in[m]$ let $f_{i}$ be the number of first place votes and
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$,
$\sum f_{i}=n$.  For $|O|\ge2$ the adversary can keep the first choice
inside $O$ and can put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$
above $O$, so that in the worst case

$\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i} ,$

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we can choose $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$-large items. Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ and

$\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}
     =\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,$

in particular $\le2t$ for $k=2$, $\le t$ for $k\ge3$ and $0$ for $k=4$.

The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.  If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$,
$n\le4t$ and $n-\max f_{i}\le3t$.  If $k=1$ after relabelling
$f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$ and no $|O|\ge2$ can be made
$>t$-loaded in the worst case.  The only worst-case admissible set is the
singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$, $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$ and

$\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,$

the bound being attained for the first place extremal profile

$f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1.$

For $t=20$

$f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\;n=81$,

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the
three other cyclic first choices.  Then $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=20<t+1$
for every pair, no pair and no triple can be made $>t$-loaded and the
unique $>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  In the
worst ranking

$c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,$

and $p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t$.  The same $n-\max f_{i}=3t$ is obtained on the
balanced $20-20-20-20$ four cycle $n=4t=80$.

Hence for every profile

$\displaystyle \min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}
          \le (m-1)t $

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$u^{*}_{\rm uni}=(m-1)t=3t$,

i.e. $u^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profiles being tight.  In the
strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book-keeping this is $u^{*}=3t+1=61$, the
usual $n-\max f_{i}\le3t$ singleton first place guarantee.  On the
conventional normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the familiar
$2(t+1)=42\approx2t=40$ pair form. ∎

2.text:
For a profile let $f_{i}$ be the number of first place votes for $i$,
$f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$, $\sum f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\#\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\ge f_{i},\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\},\;j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_{O}(i)=f_{i}$ on $O$ and can
put every voter whose first choice is outside $O$ above $O$, so that in
the worst case

$$
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
$$

and for a singleton

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge2$ we may take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$–large items and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

i.e. $\le2t$ for $k=2$ and $\le t$ for $k\ge3$.  The only $n$–free
obstruction is $k\le1$.  Then no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$ loaded in
the worst case and the only worst case admissible set is a singleton
$O_{*}=\{i_{0}\}$ with $f_{i_{0}}=\max_{i}f_{i}$.  Now

$$
p_{O_{*}}(i_{0})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{i_{0}}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t ,
\tag{*}
$$

and $(*)$ is best possible.  Indeed with

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$–loaded and the unique
$>t$–admissible set in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$.  Up to
relabelling we may take

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  Then $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}=t<t+1$ for every
pair, $p_{O^{*}}(1)=n>t$ and the adversary can make every voter whose
first choice is $2,3$ or $4$ rank the chosen outside item above $1$,
so that

$$
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=4t+1-(t+1)=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

and the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four–cycle $n=4t$ gives the same
$n-\max_{i}f_{i}=3t$.  Hence for every profile

$$
\min_{O\;>t{\rm -loaded}}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)
      \le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le (m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$–free uniform sense.  In
particular

$$
u(P)=\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le3t
$$

for every $m=4$ profile and the bound is attained on the
$t+1,t,t,t$ profile.  For $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

the unique worst case suitable set is the singleton $\{1\}$ with
$p_{\{1\}}(1)=81>20$ and

$$
c_{j}(\{1\})=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

so $60$ agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to the chosen
set and $60$ agents is best possible.  In the strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$
book–keeping this is $u_{\ge t+1}=3t+1=61$ agents, i.e. the familiar
$n-\max f_{i}\le(m-1)t$ singleton first–place guarantee.  On the
customary minimal feasible normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is
written as

$$
\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\Big\lceil\frac{n_{0}}4\Big\rceil
=t+1=21,
$$

$20$ in the loose $>t$ wording, and in pair language
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, i.e. the
usual $2t=40$ $n_{0}$–normalised form of the $3t$ uniform singleton
bound. ∎

15.text:
Write $f_{i}=|\{v:i={\rm top}(v)\}|$, $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$,
$\sum_{i}f_{i}=n$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$
p_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:i={\rm top}_{O}(v)\}\bigr|,\qquad 
c_{j}(O)=\bigl|\{v:j\succ_{v}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr| ,\;j\notin O .
$$

For $|O|\ge 2$ the $S=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i}$ voters whose first choice
lies outside $O$ can be made to have their top in $O$ where we like and
can be made to rank a prescribed $j\notin O$ above $O$.  Hence in the
worst order for the set $O$

\begin{equation*}
\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_{i},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_{i},
\end{equation*}
and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

$$
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad\max_{j\ne i}c_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}.
$$

Put $k=\#\{i:f_{i}\ge t+1\}$.  If $k\ge 2$ we may take $O$ to be the $k$
$t+1$--large first place items.  Then $\min_{i\in O}p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$
and

$$
\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_{i}\le (4-k)t,
$$

so that $k=2$ gives $\le 2t$, $k\ge3$ gives $\le t$.  The only
$n$--free obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k=0$ then $f_{i}\le t$ for all $i$, $n\le4t$ and with
$i_{0}=\arg\max f_{i}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i_{0}}c_{j}(\{i_{0}\})=n-f_{i_{0}}\le n-\Big\lceil
\frac n4\Big\rceil\le3t .
$$

If $k=1$, say $f_{1}\ge t+1$, $f_{2},f_{3},f_{4}\le t$, no $|O|\ge2$
can be made $>t$--loaded in the worst case and the only worst case
admissible set is the singleton $O_{*}=\{1\}$.  Then $p_{O_{*}}(1)=n>t$
as soon as $n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne1}c_{j}(O_{*})=n-f_{1}=f_{2}+f_{3}+f_{4}\le3t,
$$

and the bound is attainable.  The extremal first place profile is

$$
f_{1}=t+1,\qquad f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
$$

i.e. for $t=20$

$$
f_{1}=21,\;f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=20,\qquad n=81,
$$

$21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three
other cyclic first choices.  No pair has $\min\{m_{ab},m_{ba}\}\ge t+1$,
so no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$--loaded; the unique $>t$--loaded set
in the worst case is $O^{*}=\{1\}$ and

$$
p_{O^{*}}(1)=81>t,\qquad 
c_{j}(O^{*})=n-f_{1}=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
$$

$60$ agents can be forced to rank $j$ above $1$.  The balanced
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$-cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same
$n-\max f_{i}=3t$ phenomenon.  In particular

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le(m-1)t,
$$

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible in the $n$-free uniform sense.  For
$m=4$

$$
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(t)=(m-1)t=3t,
$$

i.e. $u_{\rm uni}^{*}=60$ agents for $t=20$, attained on the
$21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profiles.
In the strict $p_{O}(i)\ge t+1$ book keeping this is the familiar
$u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3(t+1)-3=61$.  On the conventional minimal feasible
normalisation $n_{0}=m(t+1)=84$ this is the usual
$\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=\lceil n_{0}/4\rceil=t+1=21$,
$\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_{j}(O)=n_{0}/2=2(t+1)=42$, i.e. the
$2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ pair form quoted in the literature. ∎

public_text.13:
The quantifier is “for all n and all strict profiles”.  Hence the guarantee has to be n-free.  
Write $f_i=|\{v: \text{top}(v)=i\}|$, $f_1\ge f_2\ge f_3\ge f_4$, $\sum f_i=n$.

For $|O|\ge 2$ the adversary can keep $p_O(i)=f_i$, $i\in O$, and can make every voter whose first choice lies outside $O$ rank that outside item above the whole of $O$. In the worst case

\[
\min_{i\in O}p_O(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_i,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i,
\]

and for a singleton $O=\{i\}$

\[
p_{\{i\}}(i)=n,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}c_j(\{i\})=n-f_i .
\]

Let $k=\#\{i:f_i\ge t+1\}$ with $t+1=21$.  If $k\ge2$ we can take $O$ to be the $k$ $t+1$-large items and

\[
\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=\sum_{i>k}f_i\le(4-k)t,
\]

so $k=2$ gives $\le2t$ and $k\ge3$ gives $\le t$.  The only $n$-free obstruction is $k\le1$.

If $k\le1$ no $|O|\ge2$ can be made $>t$-loaded in the worst case, because every such $O$ contains an $i$ with $f_i\le t$.  The only worst-case admissible set is a singleton $O_*=\{i_0\}$ with $f_{i_0}=\max_i f_i$.  Then $p_{O_*}(i_0)=n>t$ and

\[
\max_{j\ne i_0}c_j(O_*)=n-f_{i_0}=f_2+f_3+f_4\le3t .
\]

The bound is tight.  Take the first-place extremal profile

\[
f_1=t+1,\qquad f_2=f_3=f_4=t,\qquad n=4t+1,
\]

i.e. for $t=20$

\[
f_1=21,\;f_2=f_3=f_4=20,\qquad n=81,
\]

e.g. $21$ voters $1\succ2\succ3\succ4$ and $20$ voters of each of the three other cyclic first choices. The unique $>t$-admissible set in the worst case is $O^*=\{1\}$ and the adversary can make

\[
c_j(\{1\})=n-f_1=81-21=60=3t,\qquad j=2,3,4,
\]

agents rank $j$ above $1$, while $p_{\{1\}}(1)=81>t$.  The balanced $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ four-cycle $n=4t=80$ gives the same $n-\max f_i=60$.

Hence for every profile

\[
\min_O\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)\le n-\max_i f_i\le (m-1)t,
\]

and $(m-1)t$ is best possible uniformly in $n$.  In particular

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}(m,t)=(m-1)t,
\]

so for $m=4$, $t=20$,

\[
u_{\rm uni}^{*}=3t=60
\]

agents, $61$ in the strict $\ge t+1$ bookkeeping, and the $21\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$, $n=81$, profile shows necessity.  The $2t=40$, $2(t+1)=42$ numbers are the same estimate written on the conventional minimal feasible normalisation $n_0=m(t+1)=84$, i.e. $\min_{|O|=3}\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=\lceil n_0/4\rceil=t+1$ and $\min_{|O|=2}\max_{j\notin O}c_j(O)=n_0/2=2(t+1)$.  That normalisation is not part of the quantifier “for all $n$ and all profiles’’; the $n$-free uniform worst case is the singleton first-place guarantee $n-\max f_i\le3t$, i.e. $60$ for $t=20$.

$\min_{i\in O}p_O(i)=\min_{i\in O}f_i,\qquad \max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)=n-\sum_{i\in O}f_i,$

$\displaystyle \min_O\max_{j\notin O}c_O(j)\le n-\max_i f_i\le(m-1)t,$
